sonnet.problem: Card 11 just asked what believers will be when Christ appears, and its answer was 'Like Him.' Card 12 builds a True statement on that same claim, 'will be like Christ,' from the same verse, so it re-asks the fact already answered.
sonnet.rule: An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact. Two lines that make the same point get one question. An answer shown on one card, right or wrong, isn't used again on a later card.

sonnet.problem: The blank asks for the verb 'purifies.' Card 13 only says the hope-holder 'does something about himself,' so the baker has no way to reason out the word. 'Protects' and 'proves' are equally plausible, which makes it a guess at wording the baker hasn't seen.
sonnet.rule: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

sonnet.problem: The right answer, "God's seed abides in him," uses Bible-sounding wording ('abides'). The two wrong answers are plain and modern, so the right one stands out.
sonnet.rule: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
